scientific_question: For the specified chiral cyclopentadienone–iron catalyst C_A, explain how H2 hydrogenates phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanone to its chiral silyl alcohol, what controls turnover, and how catalyst organization influences formation of the two enantiomers. Predict the favored absolute configuration for this acylsilane.

inputs.content: Primary substrate: phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanone, Ph–C(=O)–Si(CH3)3; SMILES O=C(c1ccccc1)[Si](C)(C)C. The carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to silicon, not to a methylene spacer.

Primary product: phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanol, Ph–CH(OH)–Si(CH3)3; constitutional SMILES OC(c1ccccc1)[Si](C)(C)C. The carbinol carbon bears phenyl, hydroxyl, hydrogen and trimethylsilyl. Both enantiomers of this alcohol are in scope. No major-product absolute configuration is supplied; assign it from explicit product structures.

Reacting catalyst C_A is a neutral cyclopentadienone–iron tricarbonyl complex. Define the ligand graph by the ring C1(=O)–C2=C3–C4=C5–C1, with an additional C3–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2–C4 bridge. Thus the fused ring has six members. C2 and C5 each attach directly to the stereogenic C2 of a pyrrolidine ring; both pyrrolidine C2 stereocenters are S. Each pyrrolidine nitrogen is bonded to S(=O)2–Ar, where Ar is 4-phenylphenyl, with sulfur attached at aryl C1 and phenyl at C4. The iron is coordinated to the four diene carbons of the cyclopentadienone and bears three terminal carbon-bound CO ligands. The neutral tricarbonyl precatalyst has starting multiplicity 1 (singlet), supplied as the author-model boundary, not an experimental spin measurement. No optimized conformation is supplied. Subsequent species may have other justified electronic states. Direct experimental comparison for C_A uses substrate 0.2 mmol, catalyst 2 mol %, trimethylamine N-oxide 4 mol %, toluene 0.3 mL, H2 30 atm, 80 °C, 12 h. A distinct comparison catalyst C_B has the same ligand backbone and S,S stereochemistry, but Ar is 3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-methoxyphenyl, with sulfur attached at aryl C1. The optimized aryl-acylsilane comparison conditions for C_B are substrate 0.5 mmol, catalyst 2 mol %, trimethylamine N-oxide 4 mol %, H2 30 atm, iPrOH/H2O 1.2:0.3 mL, 60 °C, 12 h. C_B is observational context only: its performance must not be relabelled as a measurement for C_A, and calculations on C_B are not a required outcome.

With C_A under its toluene/H2 conditions in PI3, the primary substrate gave its alcohol in 87% yield and 86:14 enantiomeric ratio. With C_B under its optimized iPrOH/H2O/H2 conditions in PI3, the primary substrate gave its alcohol in 95% yield and 93:7 enantiomeric ratio. Yields and enantiomeric ratios are observations, not calculated answers or rate constants; no concentration-versus-time data are supplied.
